headline: PLS and FUEL lead the ASX higher today while MSFT took a decent knock last night — oil is falling on US-Iran tension easing and gold is surging past $4,174.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara bounced strongly today, up 3.1% to $5.94, as ASX lithium stocks broadly attracted buying interest. Analysts are watching whether lithium prices are forming a floor — a key test for the sector. Still down ~12% on your cost base, but today's move is an encouraging sign of renewed market attention on the space.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL jumped 2.35% today to $8.72, driven by ongoing news around US strikes in Iran and fears of Strait of Hormuz supply disruptions. Despite oil itself actually falling last night (more on that below), the geopolitical risk premium kept energy company stocks bid up on the ASX today.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft dropped 2.35% last night to $388.04 — one of its sharper single-session falls in recent months. Market chatter points to mixed sentiment around recent earnings and whether Microsoft's heavy AI investment spend is translating fast enough into revenue growth. You're now down about $49.50 AUD on this position.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two edged up 1.49% last night to $213.60. GTA 6 hype continues to simmer — fans are debating the leaked map and anticipating a third trailer. The stock remains in a positive mood as the GTA 6 release window approaches, though you're still down about $39 AUD on this one overall.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google dipped 0.8% last night to $350.50, a modest pullback. No major negative catalyst — the broader NASDAQ actually had a strong night, so this looks like mild profit-taking. Google's AI pricing cuts (see AI section) could be a long-term positive but near-term the market is digesting a lot of AI news.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI slipped a small 0.59% today to $16.91. With MSFT under pressure last night and the broader AI theme seeing some noise around regulation, the ETF drifted slightly. You're down about $22 AUD on this position overall — it's been a tough run since entry.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS eased 0.6% today to $513.40, reflecting last night's mixed US session pricing through to today's ASX trade. The S&P and NASDAQ actually had a solid night last night, so expect VTS to potentially recoup this when it reprices again tomorrow.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped a marginal 0.23% today to $90.90 — essentially flat. Emerging markets are being buffeted by US-Iran tensions and a broadly cautious mood. No major news specific to this ETF today.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG was almost perfectly flat today, down just 0.11% to $75.20. As a broadly diversified fund across global and Aussie shares, the small dip reflects the mixed day rather than any specific news. This one just does its thing quietly — all good.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Lithium bouncing, but is it real?
watch_today.detail: Pilbara jumped 3.1% today and there's a wave of analyst commentary about lithium stocks testing a price floor. That's encouraging, but the fundamental oversupply story hasn't changed yet. Hold what you have — the risk/reward doesn't justify adding more until there's a clearer signal on lithium spot prices recovering.

watch_today.title: MSFT — Took a 2.35% hit last night, worth watching
watch_today.detail: Microsoft fell 2.35% last night to $388, its sharpest single-session drop in a while, on mixed sentiment about AI spend vs revenue. You're already down ~$49.50 AUD on this position. No need to panic — MSFT's fundamentals are solid — but keep an eye on whether this selloff deepens over the next few sessions. Hold for now.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX — Geopolitical energy play still live
watch_today.detail: FUEL gained 2.35% today despite crude oil actually falling last night. The split tells you the market is pricing in geopolitical risk (US-Iran, Strait of Hormuz) separately from the short-term oil price. If the Iran situation de-escalates, FUEL could give back some of these gains. You're in the green on this one — hold and watch the news flow.

watch_today.title: Oil dropping sharply — watch the energy trade
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) fell 2.82% last night to $87.49 a barrel. Despite the US-Iran tension headlines, traders appear to be pricing in some resolution or at least less supply disruption than feared. If oil keeps sliding, FUEL.AX gains could reverse quickly. Keep an eye on this through the week.

watch_today.title: Gold surging past $4,174 — safe haven demand is real
watch_today.detail: Gold jumped 1.61% last night to $4,174 — a big move. This is the market buying safety amid US-Iran tensions and uncertainty about the US economy. You don't hold gold directly, but it signals investors are nervous, which can weigh on growth stocks like MSFT and GOOG. Good context for why markets feel jittery right now.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI regulation headwinds building globally
watch_today.detail: GXAI slipped again today and the broader AI news cycle is dominated by regulation — Trump's new AI oversight order in the US, Canada moving to regulate AI chatbots, and EU reform debates. More red tape generally means slower commercialisation for AI companies. You're down 11% on this position — hold, but don't add until there's more regulatory clarity.

markets.summary: Last night's US session was actually pretty solid — the S&P 500 gained 1.29% and the NASDAQ jumped 1.65%, suggesting the broader market is in reasonable shape. The standout moves were in commodities: gold surged to $4,174 (up 1.61%) as investors sought safety amid US-Iran tensions, while crude oil fell sharply by 2.82% to $87.49 — suggesting traders think the supply disruption risk is less severe than initially feared. The Aussie dollar held steady just above 70.3 US cents.

politics.summary: The big domestic stories today are around interest rates and the NDIS. Multiple banks are cutting home loan rates for new customers despite the RBA not yet moving, and state governments are pushing back hard on the federal government's NDIS overhaul plans.

stories.title: Banks slash home loan rates for new customers — defying the RBA
stories.why_it_matters: Several major banks are independently cutting home loan rates for new customers even though the Reserve Bank of Australia hasn't officially lowered the cash rate yet. This is banks competing for mortgage business by getting ahead of expected RBA cuts. If you're a new borrower or thinking about refinancing, now is a good time to shop around — you don't have to wait for the RBA to move. Existing variable rate customers may need to ask their bank to match new customer rates.

stories.title: Experts broadly expect the RBA's next move to be a rate cut
stories.why_it_matters: Market economists and analysts are now broadly in agreement: the RBA's next interest rate move will be a cut, not a hike. This is good news for anyone with a mortgage or variable rate debt. For investors, lower rates generally support asset prices — shares, property and bonds all tend to benefit when borrowing costs come down. The timing is still uncertain, but the direction of travel looks clear.

stories.title: Fears the RBA won't be able to cut rates if recession hits
stories.why_it_matters: There's a counter-argument worth knowing: some economists worry that if Australia tips into a recession (two consecutive quarters of economic contraction), the RBA may have already used up its rate-cutting firepower or face constraints that limit how much it can cut. This is a tail risk — not the base case — but it's worth keeping in mind when reading optimistic rate-cut headlines.

stories.title: State governments warn Canberra: we can't replace NDIS services for those cut off
stories.why_it_matters: State and territory disability ministers have united to warn the Albanese government that they simply cannot provide 'like-for-like' services for the thousands of people who will be removed from the NDIS under the federal overhaul. The states are saying they don't have the funding or infrastructure to pick up the slack. This is shaping up as a major political fight between Canberra and the states, with real consequences for people with disability and their families.

ai.summary: The AI story today is dominated by two things: Google aggressively cutting its AI API prices to undercut competitors, and a wave of new government regulation — Trump in the US, Canada, and ongoing EU debates. Plus, Anthropic's new Claude Fable 5 model is going head-to-head with GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro.

stories.title: Google slashes AI prices — bad news for OpenAI and Anthropic
stories.why_it_matters: Google has cut the prices it charges developers to use its AI models through its API (the programming interface businesses use to build AI-powered apps). The cuts are significant enough to put real pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic, who charge more for comparable capabilities. For Google (GOOG), this is a land-grab strategy — sacrifice margin now to win market share. It's a bullish long-term signal for Alphabet's AI business, even if it compresses short-term revenue. You hold GOOG, so this is worth watching.

stories.title: Trump signs new AI executive order — could reshape how models are launched in the US
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump has signed a new executive order that would change the rules around how AI companies like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic can release new models in the US. The details are still emerging, but it signals the 'hands-off' era of US AI regulation is ending. More oversight could slow the pace of new model launches and add compliance costs for the big AI players — relevant for your GOOG and GXAI.AX holdings.

stories.title: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 takes on GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic has released Claude Fable 5, its latest flagship model, and benchmarks show it's now genuinely competitive with OpenAI's GPT-5.5 and Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro — particularly in image understanding tasks. This is the AI arms race in real-time: three companies all roughly neck-and-neck on capability. For everyday users, the practical upshot is that all three top AI assistants are now extremely capable at reading and analysing images, charts, and documents — not just text.

stories.title: Canada moves to regulate social media and AI chatbots
stories.why_it_matters: Canada has introduced legislation targeting both social media platforms and AI chatbots, requiring them to meet new standards around content and transparency. It's part of a global regulatory wave — alongside the EU AI Act and Trump's new US order — that's tightening the rules for AI companies. More compliance requirements globally means higher costs for the big tech platforms, which is a headwind worth watching for GOOG and MSFT.

sport.summary: Big NRL night — the Rabbitohs demolished the Broncos 48-6 in an emotional Round 15 opener at Accor Stadium, with Jai Arrow's return the emotional centrepiece. Dolphins host the Roosters tomorrow night at Suncorp. AFL has a few stories bubbling too.

stories.title: Rabbitohs smash Broncos 48-6 in emotional Round 15 opener
stories.why_it_matters: The Rabbitohs ran riot at Accor Stadium on Thursday night, belting the Broncos 48-6 in a performance that had the whole ground emotional. The catalyst was the return of Jai Arrow, whose story had players and fans alike trying not to cry. Campbell Johnston was also outstanding, bringing the crowd to its feet. For the Broncos, it's now six straight losses and they're copping real heat — they were down two players to injury during the match, adding to the misery.

stories.title: Broncos' miserable run continues — six straight losses and double injury blow
stories.why_it_matters: The Broncos copped a double injury blow during the 48-6 thrashing, making a horror night even worse. Six consecutive losses is a crisis point for any NRL club — Brisbane will need to seriously examine their form and roster heading into the second half of the season. The Dolphins host the Roosters tomorrow night at Suncorp, giving local Gold Coast fans another reason to tune in.

stories.title: SA locks in AFL Gather Round until 2029
stories.why_it_matters: South Australia has secured AFL Gather Round — the festival round where all 18 clubs play in Adelaide over one weekend — until at least 2029. The deal is locked in but venue decisions are still being finalised. It's a big win for South Australian tourism and the Adelaide AFL clubs, and cements Gather Round as a permanent fixture on the AFL calendar.

stories.title: World Cup wagering — bigger than 30 Super Bowls or 20 AFL grand finals
stories.why_it_matters: A fascinating piece on the scale of World Cup betting — the article claims the FIFA World Cup generates the equivalent wagering value of 30 Super Bowls or 20 AFL grand finals combined, making it the single most valuable sporting event for the global betting industry. With the 2026 World Cup coming up, sports betting platforms and media companies are gearing up for massive revenue opportunities.
